text.p: Scientific-Atlanta Inc said Monday it expects to have production units of its MainGate two-way interactive energy automation system available in the first quarter.

As previously announced, Florida Progress Corp's Florida Power Corp subsidiary plans to launch a 1,000-point pilot program before the end of this year that includes both residential and commercial buildings.
Scientific-Atlanta said its MainGate system will supply the communications applications for the program, which is scheduled to be fully installed by the end of first quarter.

The company said MainGate will enable electric utilities to adapt to each of the currently available local area network communications protocols, such as CEBus and Echelon LonWorks, allowing for future application enhancements and support by multiple suppliers.

The MainGate system resides at the customer site and facilitates communication between the utility and end use devices such as an electric meter or a thermostat, or between the utility and consumer interfaces, such as an enhanced programmable thermostat or a television.
The system's open architecture allows flexibility in the number and type of applications that can be provided as well as communications protocols, Scientific-Atlanta noted.

"We are very excited about our MainGate system because we feel that it addresses real needs within the electric utility industry," said Jack King, president of Scientific-Atlanta's Control Systems Division. "We have developed MainGate around an open architecture so that third party applications can be readily adapted to offer a full range of value-added products and services."

By utilizing communications networks such as hybrid fiber/coax, satellite and wireless UHF/VHF radio, the MainGate system is capable of supporting basic applications such as automatic meter reading, service connect and disconnect, tamper detection, outage detection, customer-controlled load management and real-time pricing. In addition, the communications infrastructure will allow for adding data services, security monitoring, telephony, entertainment and other interactive services in the future.
